sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Lübeck raised street parking fees sharply on 1 June 2025 and has been closing routes into its island centre. The new fee ordinance replaced the 2008 one with five zones, raising fees where use is heavy, such as the Altstadtinsel and Travemünde, while peripheral car parks stay cheaper [0]. The Altstadt costs €3.00 an hour and the day ticket was abolished [3]. The Brötchentaste (free short stay) was extended from 10 to 15 minutes, and free parking for electric vehicles runs to the end of 2026 [0][2]. The CDU, Greens and FDP asked the supervisory authority in May 2025 whether the mayor may raise fees without the Bürgerschaft, and the mayor said he may [3]. Resident permits now cost €90 a year, under an ordinance signed on 28 August 2026 and in force from 1 September [6].

Access to the centre is also being squeezed by closures. The Hubbrücke over the canal has been closed to cars since 9 February 2023, with an overhaul estimated at €40 million [9]. The Mühlentorbrücke, the access from the south, was closed to all traffic on 5 December 2025 after an inspection rated its condition inadequate [10]. The upper Beckergrube is being redesigned, with works due to finish in autumn 2026 [8]. In December 2025 access via Große Burgstraße was banned from 10:30 to 22:00 for the Christmas market, with a €50 fine [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Most of the city's public parking is run by KWL, which lists 76 locations in Lübeck and Travemünde, only some with live counts [13]. Several garages are in flux. Parkhaus Am Holstentor was closed from 31 December 2025 because continued operation was no longer possible [19], and it is to be demolished and replaced, with construction planned from the first quarter of 2027, opening expected in the third quarter of 2028 and construction costs of about €13.2 million (planned figures) [20]. Kanalstraße P1 was closed from 1 September 2025 for a modular school building for an expected five years [22]. Parkhaus Falkenstraße reopened in September 2025 after an investment of over €4 million to repair corrosion [18].

Travemünde is the other focus. The Parkhaus Godewind opened on 28 March 2025 with 301 spaces at €2.00 an hour [16], but its first review found monthly utilisation between 6.7% and 16.7% and a 2025 loss of about €641,000, of which Lübeck indirectly bears 80%. It peaked at 90% during the Travemünder Woche [17]. A parking concept for Travemünde is being prepared [25]. During the Travemünder Woche in July 2026 KWL listed Am Fischereihafen and Backbord at €1.60 per 30 minutes, the Kowitzberg lot as free, and about 300 of 750 spaces at Leuchtenfeld [23]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Lübeck data cover ten car parks with 2,130 spaces, and they are two different markets. Six are in the Lübeck city centre, with 1,091 spaces: Kanalstraße P3 to P5, Lastadie P5, the MuK and the lot at the Radisson Blu Senator Hotel. KWL lists the MuK at €1.20 per 30 minutes and €8 a day, Monday to Saturday from 10:00 to 18:00 [14]; we did not confirm the same tariff for the others. Four are in Travemünde, with 1,039 spaces: Am Fischereihafen, Backbord, Hafenbahnhof and the Kowitzberg lot. The ordinance puts the first three in Zone IV, where KWL lists €1.60 per 30 minutes and a €12 day ticket, and Kowitzberg is free [2][13][23].

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 51% on weekdays and 57% at weekends in the city-centre lots, and 13% and 16% in the Travemünde ones. The fullest are the Radisson Blu lot (86%), Kanalstraße P4 (83%), P3 and P5 (both 70%). The MuK (31%) and Lastadie P5 (37%) are far quieter. In Travemünde, Hafenbahnhof is at 67% on weekdays, while Am Fischereihafen (19%), Backbord (15%) and Kowitzberg (1%, a free lot) are almost empty in our window, which falls after the Travemünder Woche. Capacities in our feed differ from KWL's page, for example Kanalstraße P3 at 196 against 122, so its percentage should be read with care. Over the years Kanalstraße P3 fell from 87% in 2022 to 70% in 2025, Lastadie P5 from 53% to 42%, and Kowitzberg from 24% to 3%. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ.
